raw_response:
I've been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life. My two sons went to work in Baoding years ago, so it's just me and my wife now. I farm about 10 mu — my own contracted plot plus a few mu I took over from old neighbor Chen when he moved away. My back isn't what it was, so I rely on the village machinery cooperative for the big jobs.

There's no question what I'll grow. Wheat in winter, corn in summer. That's what I've done for 40 years. That's what the grain station takes. That's what I know.

For wheat, I'll sow the Jimai 22 variety — it's what the seed shop in town has been selling for years and my yields have been decent. I put down compound fertilizer when I seed, then top-dress with urea at jointing. Wheat needs water here — this land is dry. I'll run the pump at least four times: once before winter sets in to help the roots, again at jointing, heading, and grain-filling. I'll spray herbicide once in spring and a fungicide when I see rust starting to come in, like most years.

For corn, I'll direct-seed right after the wheat combine comes through in June — no time to waste. I use Zhengdan 958, buy new seed every year from the co-op. Corn in summer gets some rain but I'll irrigate once or twice if it stays dry at silking. I put fertilizer in at planting and topdress once more when it's knee-high. Not much spraying needed for corn usually — maybe once if aphids get bad.

I'm not changing anything this year. The price of wheat and corn is stable enough, and at my age I'm not going to start experimenting.
